outcomeNote: A baraita expounds the mishna's verse.

segments.he: ״מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה כּוּ׳״, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אֲשֶׁר אֵרַס״, אֶחָד הַמְאָרֵס אֶת הַבְּתוּלָה, וְאֶחָד הַמְאָרֵס אֶת הָאַלְמָנָה, וְאֶחָד שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם. וַאֲפִילּוּ חֲמִשָּׁה אַחִין, וּמֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם בַּמִּלְחָמָה — כּוּלָּן חוֹזְרִין. ״לֹא לָקַח״, ״וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ״ — פְּרָט לְאַלְמָנָה לַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט, מַמְזֶרֶת וּנְתִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַמְזֵר וּלְנָתִין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches among the statements that were said before battle: «“What man is there that has betrothed a wife» and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house” (Deuteronomy 20:7). «The Sages taught: “That has betrothed”» is referring to «one who betroths a virgin, and» to «one who betroths a widow, and» to «one» whose yevama is «a widow awaiting her yavam,» i.e., this man in the military ranks, to perform levirate marriage. «And even» if there are «five brothers, and one of them dies in the war, they all return» for the widow. In addition, the verse could have singled out one who has «not taken» a wife. When the verse specifies: «“and has not taken her,”» this «excludes» men in forbidden marriages: «A widow» who is betrothed «to a High Priest;» either «a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza],» who is betrothed «to a common priest; a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman» who is betrothed «to an Israelite;» or «an Israelite woman» who is betrothed «to a mamzer or to a Gibeonite.»

moves.summary: Virgin, widow and yevama all included; five brothers all return.
'And has not taken her' excludes forbidden betrothals.

edges.about: 'that has betrothed' covers virgin, widow and a yevama awaiting levirate marriage
'and has not taken her' excludes forbidden betrothals

positions.claim: betrothal of a virgin, a widow, or a yevama awaiting levirate marriage all exempt; even five brothers all return; forbidden betrothals do not exempt
